title: Two cities, one team
setting: Agile payments team split between Lisbon and Manila, seven hours apart, in two-week sprints. The team sets its own working agreements, and company policy says all overtime must be logged and approved.

steps.line: I'm Kofi, Scrum Master for a payments team. Four developers are in Lisbon, and three are in Manila, seven hours ahead.
Bea is the product owner. The team sets its own working agreements. Company policy says all overtime must be logged and approved.
Sprint review and planning both start at three in the afternoon, Lisbon time. That's ten at night in Manila.
Carlo, in Manila, messages me privately. He's exhausted, and he feels the Lisbon side doesn't care.
Before talking with the team, I email both line managers and ask them to settle the meeting times between them.

error.summary: Escalated to line managers before working it out with the team
error.why: Bringing in managers is reasonable if the team can't resolve it, but it comes too early. Meeting times are a working agreement the team can set. Listen first and try the lowest level before escalating.
error.correctAction: Talk with Carlo first to understand the problem, then bring the time-zone issue to the whole team to agree a fairer rhythm. Escalate only if they can't.
error.consequence: The managers swapped emails for a week and then imposed a time nobody liked. Carlo felt his private message had been passed up the chain.

steps.line: I ask Carlo for ten minutes to hear more, and thank him for telling me directly.
In a short call with everyone, I share a chart of working hours. There are only two hours a day when both cities overlap.
I write up a new meeting schedule myself and post it in the channel as the team's final working agreement.

error.summary: Imposed a working agreement instead of facilitating one
error.why: A working agreement only works if the team makes it. Posting a final schedule takes the decision away from a self-managing team and skips the people most affected.
error.correctAction: Bring two or three options to the team, such as rotating times or recorded demos, and help them choose one and try it for a sprint.
error.consequence: Two Lisbon developers ignored the new times, the Manila side still felt unheard, and integration bugs from a missed planning session cost the team its next sprint goal.

steps.line: I suggest we try recorded demos, so Manila can watch the review the next morning and add comments.
For this Friday, I ask the Manila developers to join the ten p.m. review anyway, and keep it off their timesheets since it's only an hour.

error.summary: Asked the team to work unlogged overtime
error.why: Company policy says overtime must be logged and approved, and labour law protects working hours. Asking people to hide hours misreports their work and treats them unfairly.
error.correctAction: Don't ask for hidden hours. Move or record Friday's review, or get the overtime approved and logged through the normal route.
error.consequence: An HR audit found unlogged late-night hours on the team. The company had to back-pay overtime, and Kofi was formally warned for breaching policy.

steps.line: At the next retrospective, we'll check whether the new rhythm is working for both cities.
